messages:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — sketching a new set of heuristics for max tokens-per-batch and GPU token-slicing. Goal: keep P95 latency under 120ms for 8k-context models while maximizing throughput. Posting quick rationale + numbers we used in profiling.

Alex Chen: TL;DR recommendations (starting point, per-GPU):
```
H100: 32768
A100: 24576
A10 : 16384
L4  : 12288
T4  : 8192
```
Rationale: kernel fit + KV cache fragmentation. These were chosen so kernel selector stays on the fast large-kernel path for most seq-length mixes and so we avoid eviction pressure in the KV slab allocator.

Maya Gupta: Nice. A couple questions: 1) how are we accounting for "kv-hot" requests with long prefixes? 2) Are these absolute caps or soft targets that the queue can override?

Alex Chen: Good q. Planning to treat them as soft budget targets. Queue will try to fill up to the target but we allow a short-tail hold window (20–30ms) to hit the target if the headroom looks sustainable. For kv-hot: if kv_hot_ratio > 0.6 we apply a reduction factor (start at 0.75) to avoid fragmentation-induced kernel slowdowns.

Samir Patel: FYI saw a perf regression on an A10 run yesterday when batch token >16k — kernel selector picked an int8 fused-kernel that regresses latency for certain seq distributions. Log: 
```
[2026-03-15T22:13:02Z] selector: chosen_kernel=int8_fused_v2, p95_ms=210, expected_p95=110
```
We should add a kernel-fallback rule keyed by p95 over a sliding window.

Jenna Ortiz: Agreed. Also we should gate these changes behind canaries. Suggest rollout plan: 5% traffic for 24h -> check P95, P99, reject rate, kv eviction metrics -> 25% -> 100%. Add a kill-switch if reject_rate > 0.5% or kv_evictions/sec spikes 3x.

Kai O'Neill: Can we attach per-model profiles? A single GPU cap is noisy because 4k-context vs 32k-context models behave differently. Idea: keep default per-GPU bucket but allow model-specific overrides (model_profile_id -> max_tokens_per_batch).

Alex Chen: Yep — plan is default bucket + optional model override table stored in runtime config. We already have model fingerprinting in the router. Implementation notes:
```
- runtime config: { default_buckets: {...}, overrides: {model_id: token_budget, ...} }
- queue logic: compute target = overrides[model] || default[gpu_type]
- if kv_hot_ratio>0.6 then target *= 0.75
- if kernel_selector.history[p95] > 150ms -> scale target down 0.6
- hold_window_ms = 25
```

Maya Gupta: What about memory OOM risk when multiple large batches land on same GPU? Do we need a global in-flight token cap per-device?

Samir Patel: Yes, add device_token_ceiling = floor(GPU_mem_gb / model_mem_per_token) * safety_margin. Practically we can set an in-flight token ceiling to ensure no OOM even during synchronized bursts. If ceiling reached, queue should force-ship smaller batches.

infra-bot: Profiling summary uploaded: https://internal.redwood/profiles/1755554321/ (contains A10/A100/H100 runs, seed workloads, KV occupancy heatmaps). Auto-tag: perf/regression/p95-checks.

Jenna Ortiz: For rollout metrics add these dashboards: per-device p50/p95/p99, kernel_selector.choice_pct, kv_evictions/sec, in_flight_token_count, reject_rate. We'll watch tail latency especially during burst windows.

Kai O'Neill: Small request — include an experiment that forces kernel_selector to prefer fp16 kernel on A10 for batches >12k (to avoid the int8_fused_v2 regression Samir mentioned). We can flip it per-canary.

Alex Chen: Will do. Action items:
- Samir: add kernel fallback rule + alert when p95 > 150ms for 10m window.
- Jenna: create canary rollout in release playbook (5%/24h/25%/100%) + dashboards.
- Maya: add KV-hot heuristic tests (kv_hot_ratio sim workload).
- Kai: prototype model-specific config table + test override.
- infra-bot: keep profiling link pinned to thread.

Alex Chen: I'll iterate on numbers after the first canary. If anyone has objections to the bucket values above please shout now, otherwise I'll add this to the runtime PR and wire the config flags. :thumbsup:
